quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.subtitle: Learn how to use CrossResearch to understand what is moving markets, identify opportunities and build a structured market view.

blocks.text: CrossResearch brings macroeconomic data, market expectations, positioning, options analytics, seasonality, market intelligence and technical tools into one research environment.
The objective is not to tell you what to buy or sell. CrossResearch is designed to help you answer the questions that should come before a trading decision.
Before entering a market, you should understand:
What is happening in the economy?
What could change the current narrative?
Does price action confirm the thesis?
CrossResearch helps organize these questions into a repeatable research process.
A simple way to use the platform is:
Start with the economic and market environment.
Study expectations, positioning, flows and important market levels.
Use market structure and technical indicators to determine whether price action supports the thesis.
Only then decide whether the opportunity matches your own strategy and risk management.
If you are new to CrossResearch, follow this order:
You do not need every tool to agree before taking a trade. The objective is to understand the complete market environment rather than relying on a single indicator.

what-is-crossresearch.title: What is CrossResearch?
what-is-crossresearch.subtitle: A research platform designed to help traders understand the forces driving financial markets.

blocks.text: Financial markets are influenced by several layers at the same time.

Economic growth may be improving while inflation is falling. Central banks may be becoming more dovish. Institutional positioning may already be heavily bullish. Options markets may contain important levels around current price.
Looking at only one of these variables provides an incomplete picture.
CrossResearch brings these different layers together.
Understand growth, inflation, employment, monetary policy and economic momentum.
Understand what investors already expect before economic events or policy decisions.
Understand how different groups of market participants are positioned.
Identify areas where options exposure and dealer hedging may influence price behaviour.
Study recurring historical tendencies across different markets and periods.
Use CrossResearch TradingView indicators to analyze trends, momentum, liquidity and important technical structures.
Follow important economic, geopolitical and market-moving developments.
CrossResearch does not guarantee market outcomes.
A bullish indicator does not automatically mean price will rise.
A bearish indicator does not automatically mean price will fall.
Every signal should be interpreted within the broader market environment.

navigating-crossresearch.title: Navigating CrossResearch
navigating-crossresearch.subtitle: Understand how the different areas of the platform work together.

blocks.text: The CrossResearch platform is organized into research modules. Each module answers a different market question.
Use Macro tools to understand the economic environment.
Use positioning tools to understand how market participants are positioned and whether exposure is becoming crowded.
Use options analytics to identify important strikes, dealer gamma conditions and potential areas of support, resistance or price attraction.
Use CrossResearch indicators directly on price charts to analyze market structure, momentum and liquidity.
Use News and Geopolitical tools to understand catalysts capable of changing the current market narrative.
Use the Education Center and documentation whenever you encounter a concept you do not understand.
Different datasets update at different frequencies.
Always check the Last Updated value shown on the relevant tool before interpreting the data.
Some economic datasets update monthly or quarterly, while options, market prices and news may update much more frequently.

daily-research-routine.subtitle: A simple process for using CrossResearch before the trading session.

macro-nowcast.title: Macro Nowcast
macro-nowcast.subtitle: Estimate current economic conditions before traditional economic statistics fully confirm them.

blocks.text: Economic statistics are usually released with a delay.
GDP, inflation, employment and other economic indicators describe economic activity that has already occurred.
A nowcast uses currently available information to estimate the present state of the economy.
Markets frequently move before official economic statistics confirm a change.

macro-signals.title: Macro Signals
macro-signals.subtitle: Transform large amounts of economic information into easier-to-read directional signals.

blocks.text: Macro Signals summarize groups of economic variables into higher-level information.
Instead of monitoring dozens of individual indicators independently, the signal helps identify whether a macro theme is strengthening or weakening.
A positive signal generally indicates improving momentum in the underlying factor.
A negative signal generally indicates deteriorating momentum.
Neutral conditions suggest that no sufficiently strong directional signal currently exists.

cot-market-positioning.title: COT & Market Positioning
cot-market-positioning.subtitle: Understand how major groups of futures market participants are positioned.

blocks.text: The Commitments of Traders report provides information about futures positioning across different groups of market participants.
Is the market already heavily positioned for this idea?
A strong trend with increasing positioning can indicate confirmation.
Extremely crowded positioning may indicate increased reversal risk.
Extreme positioning is not automatically contrarian.
A market can remain heavily positioned in one direction for an extended period.
Always combine positioning with price behaviour and macro conditions.

options-positioning.title: Options Positioning
options-positioning.subtitle: Understand how options exposure may influence important market levels and intraday behaviour.

blocks.text: Options markets contain information about how traders and dealers are positioned across different strikes and expirations.
CrossResearch converts this information into practical market levels.
A Call Wall identifies an area with significant call-related positioning.
Depending on market conditions, it may behave as an important resistance, attraction or positioning level.
A Put Wall identifies an area with significant put-related positioning.
It may behave as an important support or positioning level.
The Gamma Flip represents an approximate level where the broader dealer gamma environment may change.
Above and below this area, hedging behaviour may differ.
The Primary Pin represents a strike or price area where options positioning may encourage price concentration, particularly near expiration.
Positive dealer gamma is commonly associated with more stabilizing hedging behaviour.
Negative gamma environments can create more destabilizing hedging behaviour.
These relationships are tendencies rather than guarantees.

seasonality-flow.title: Seasonality & Flow
seasonality-flow.subtitle: Study recurring historical behaviour and changes in market participation.

blocks.text: Seasonality identifies patterns that have historically occurred during certain periods.
It does not predict the future with certainty.
Flow measures changes in market participation.
It can help identify whether capital is moving into or out of a market.
These concepts are related but different.

geopolitical-intelligence.title: Geopolitical Intelligence
geopolitical-intelligence.subtitle: Understand how geopolitical developments can transmit into financial markets.

blocks.text: Geopolitical events rarely affect every market in the same way.
Conflict → Oil Supply Risk → Higher Oil → Inflation Risk → Interest Rate Expectations
Shipping Disruption → Higher Freight Costs → Higher Input Costs → Inflation Pressure
The objective is not simply to classify an event as bullish or bearish.
The objective is to understand how the event can reach financial markets.

crossresearch-tradingview-indicators.subtitle: Turn CrossResearch market research into actionable chart context directly inside TradingView.

TradingView Indicators → Understand Where and When

trend-structure.title: Trend Structure
trend-structure.subtitle: Identify the dominant market structure and changes in directional behaviour.

blocks.text: Trend Structure helps determine whether price is behaving within a bullish, bearish or neutral structure.
Am I trading with the current market structure or against it?
A bullish macro thesis combined with bullish price structure provides stronger confirmation than a bullish macro thesis while price remains structurally bearish.

break-of-structure-volume.title: Break of Structure & Volume
break-of-structure-volume.subtitle: Identify structural breaks and evaluate whether market participation supports them.

blocks.text: A Break of Structure occurs when price moves beyond an important previous structural level.
Price breaks above an important previous swing high.
Price breaks below an important previous swing low.
Not every break is equally significant.
Volume can provide additional information about the level of participation behind a move.
A structural breakout accompanied by stronger participation may carry more information than a breakout occurring during weak activity.
A Break of Structure is not automatically a trade entry.

multi-timeframe-momentum.title: Multi-Timeframe Momentum
multi-timeframe-momentum.subtitle: Compare directional momentum across multiple timeframes.

blocks.text: Markets can be bullish on one timeframe while bearish on another.
This may represent a shorter-term correction within a larger bullish trend.
The timeframe you trade should determine which signals receive the most importance.
An intraday trader may care more about short-term momentum.
A swing trader may prioritize 4H and daily conditions.
When multiple relevant timeframes point in the same direction, directional conviction may increase.
Mixed readings indicate that the market does not currently have clean timeframe alignment.

liquidity-delta-matrix.title: Liquidity & Delta Matrix
liquidity-delta-matrix.subtitle: Identify areas where liquidity and buying or selling pressure may be concentrated.

blocks.text: Markets frequently move toward areas where significant liquidity exists.
The Liquidity & Delta Matrix helps visualize where market participation is concentrated and whether aggressive buying or selling pressure is dominant.
Liquidity refers to areas where significant orders or market interest may exist.
These areas can become important targets or reaction zones.
Delta compares aggressive buying activity with aggressive selling activity.
Positive delta indicates stronger aggressive buying.
Negative delta indicates stronger aggressive selling.
Price and delta do not always move together.

combining-indicators.title: Combining Indicators
combining-indicators.subtitle: Use independent forms of confirmation instead of searching for a perfect indicator.

blocks.text: The indicators are designed to answer different questions.
What direction is the market structure?
Has an important structural level been broken with participation?
Do multiple timeframes support the move?

This represents stronger alignment than relying on any one indicator independently.

indicator-settings.title: Indicator Settings
indicator-settings.subtitle: Adjust indicators to your timeframe and trading style without over-optimizing them.

blocks.text: Different markets and timeframes behave differently.
Short-term traders typically require more responsive settings.
Longer-term traders generally require more stable signals.
Avoid constantly changing settings to make historical charts look perfect.
The objective is not to produce an indicator that predicted every historical move.
The objective is to use consistent tools that provide useful information in real time.

faq.title: Faq
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions about using CrossResearch.

blocks.text: I would implement these exact questions:
Does CrossResearch tell me what to buy or sell?
No. CrossResearch provides research, data and analytical tools designed to help users form their own market views.
Bullish indicates that the relevant indicator currently favours upward conditions. It does not guarantee price will rise.
Bearish indicates that the relevant indicator currently favours downward conditions. It does not guarantee price will fall.
Why did the market move opposite to the economic data?
Markets respond to expectations rather than simply whether an economic number appears good or bad.
Positioning, monetary policy expectations and existing market pricing can also influence the reaction.
Why does the CrossResearch Nowcast differ from the official number?
A nowcast is an estimate produced before all official information becomes available.
It is expected to evolve as new information arrives.
Why does positioning data sometimes look delayed?
Some positioning datasets, including regulatory futures positioning reports, are released on a fixed schedule rather than in real time.
Does extreme positioning mean I should trade the opposite direction?
Extreme positioning indicates that a trade may be crowded, but trends can remain crowded for long periods.
Are options levels guaranteed support or resistance?
They represent areas where options positioning may influence market behaviour.
Can I use one CrossResearch signal by itself?
You can inspect signals independently, but CrossResearch is designed around combining multiple forms of evidence.
Which tools are most useful for intraday trading?
Economic Calendar, Options Positioning, News, TradingView indicators, liquidity and momentum tools are generally the most relevant.
Which tools are most useful for swing trading?
Macro Nowcast, Macro Signals, Positioning, Seasonality and higher-timeframe TradingView indicators become more important.
Relationships between assets depend on the economic regime and market narrative.
Correlations are dynamic rather than permanent.
